source.title: Gradient-Coherent Strong Regularization for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: D. Park; Chiu-Man Ho; Yi Chang; Hua-Qing Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training under strong L1/L2 regularization with a proposed gradient-coherence method and reports learning failure and recovery. Its relevant results do not measure training classification error, so they do not directly test the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation/test accuracy and training loss, but not training classification error. The training-loss result is recorded under fits_no_version because it describes learning failure without measuring the classification-error outcome named in the versions. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures regularization-induced training-loss stalls, gradient suppression, and validation/test accuracy. It does not measure V1's training classification error or directly test V2–V6. Its initialization, normalization, and Fixup discussion supplies no original comparison on those versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors attribute learning failure under sufficiently strong L1/L2 regularization to gradient suppression and propose selective or delayed regularization to avoid it. They report improved accuracy in most tested comparisons and compression up to 9.9×; accuracy improvements are not universal or uniformly statistically significant.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SGD with momentum and L1/L2 regularization, comparing fixed regularization against a proposed gradient-coherence rule. The text does not state the initialization recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Regularization strength and network depth change when baseline learning fails; the reported tolerance level decreases as hidden layers are added on SVHN.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-16 on CIFAR-100 has no decrease in training loss with L2 regularization at λ = 0.002. Delaying regularization avoids the baseline's exponential decay in loss-gradient magnitude.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong regularization applied from the start can stall optimization through gradient suppression; delaying its onset can prevent that suppression.

record.problems: The relevant reported failure is training loss, not training classification error. The paper's principal accuracy results are presented as accuracy rather than training error; the specific Figure 2a training-loss comparison gives no uncertainty estimate.
record.rows_left_out: No other result rows bear directly on training classification error. The paper's validation/test accuracy table and figures, sparsity/compression results, and results on SVHN do not measure the behavior named by the listed versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including near-zero error and substantial residual error under regularization; corrupted labels, model-size effects, and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized networks and prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization comparisons, training speed attributable to initialization, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The SVHN depth sweep concerns regularization tolerance inferred from held-out accuracy, not V3's training-error comparison. Training-loss and gradient findings do not justify verdicts on training classification error.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model-size effects, early stopping, and comparisons of SGD with Adam are not reported.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student width sweep or spurious-minimum result.
No plain versus residual shortcut comparison.
No initialization comparison or trainable-depth sweep.
No learning-rate stability or sharpness results.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Train with L2 regularization using the baseline recipe.
rows.value: Training loss does not decrease at all.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes training loss stalling; it does not report training classification error.
rows.check: The reported training-loss stall is accurately extracted, but it does not establish the training classification error named by V1. The state cannot be observed relative to any listed version.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Train with the proposed gradient-coherent strong-regularization method.
rows.baseline: Baseline at λ = 2 × 10−3: exponential decay in |∇L|.
rows.value: The proposed model obtains great elevation instead of exponential decay in |∇L|.
rows.note: The authors interpret this gradient result as evidence that their method does not fail to learn; it is not a training-classification-error measure.
rows.check: Gradient magnitude cannot establish any version's behavioral outcome. This is a diagnostic comparison of the proposed method with its baseline and should remain only under fits_no_version. Figure 8 uses the delayed-regularization method, with regularization starting after five epochs, rather than the per-step coherence rule.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
